requiredFindings.title: The SEAL-path hold leaves no release when COMMIT is not called
requiredFindings.failureScenario: Item 5 step 7 now holds level 4 through staging, X4's repeated checkpoint and AdmissionPermit, and the evidence COMMIT, until that COMMIT returns Committed or CommitUndetermined, then releases. Level 3 is never acquired under level 4, and the ledger transaction is acquired before level 4. That is the path that reaches COMMIT, and it matches X3c r2 item 8, X4 r4 item 3, and the build plan. The same exception is the only SEAL release. An uncertain journal barrier says no evidence commit proceeds. A staging abort (X3c item 6) commits nothing. Item 10's journal half of F19, after a failed post-SEAL checkpoint, releases level 4 then level 3 and appends REV through a fresh level-3 then level-4 call. The build plan's F19 and F38 require that release. Step 7's wait does not fire when COMMIT is not called, so the in-process JournalAppendLock stays held and the fresh REV acquire cannot run. X3c r2 forbids releasing level 4 before the evidence commit. Item 7 of X3c names the outcomes success and CommitUndetermined; Committed is not one of them. Required: on the path that calls the evidence COMMIT, level 4 stays held until COMMIT returns success or CommitUndetermined, then is released. If the SEAL path stops before the evidence COMMIT (uncertain journal barrier, staging abort, or checkpoint or AdmissionPermit refusal), level 4 is released at that stop, before any fresh level-3 then level-4 REV. Step 7 and item 10 must state that same release. Level 3 is never acquired or reacquired under level 4.

requiredFindings.title: PROPOSAL-r4.md is not the accepted r4 subject
requiredFindings.failureScenario: The r5 header says the r4 bytes are preserved in PROPOSAL-r4.md. The accepted X3b r4 subject is 24340 bytes, sha256 296c05673cb535aec3d363f6ff908ef3d7011b2351d6322b67c47fa492c4a156. PROPOSAL-r4.md is 24375 bytes, sha256 304a679055ba3fc4b4fbf5ff2ea2ecf09246c303b0cc724e85c0c21f4754a4b9. The difference is the inserted date-paragraph sentence "r4 ACCEPTED by Grok on 2026-09-30. "; deleting it restores the accepted hash. r5's date paragraph carries that same insertion, so r5 is the stamped copy plus the step-7 amendment. Required: PROPOSAL-r4.md is the accepted bytes, and r5's date paragraph does not carry that insertion. The r5 provenance line may record that r4 was accepted.

scope: Law X3b r5 paired with X3c r2. The SEAL hold through a COMMIT that returns is present. RF-1: stops before that COMMIT have no level-4 release. RF-2: PROPOSAL-r4.md is the accepted r4 text plus a 35-byte acceptance stamp. No product cargo.
